extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners, patent applicants, and patent agents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how Korean Patent Office examiners may make ex‑officio amendments, the notification/opposition and re‑examination procedures, and rules and procedures for preliminary examination interviews between examiners and applicants/agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "obvious mistakes" (Article 66(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'obvious mistake' in a specification, drawing(s) or abstract means a person skilled in the art should easily recognize the mistake and it is easily anticipated how the documents are to be amended because the applicant's original intention can be clearly understood from the specification, written arguments and common general technical knowledge as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to specification, drawings, and abstract. The examiner must be able to clearly infer applicant's original intention from the filed record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ex-officio amendment (general principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex-officio amendment is permitted only for obvious mistakes and is intended to correct simple clerical or obvious errors so as to prevent delay and make the specification free of mistakes; it is an exception and should be applied complementally, not broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although scope was extended (from March 2017) to allow correction of deficiencies that would otherwise be grounds for rejection if they are obvious mistakes, a decision to grant will be revoked if applicant does not agree with ex‑officio amendment. Examiners must be cautious because Article 47 strictly defines who may amend and the scope/time limits for amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of matters amendable ex‑officio (high-level list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters amendable include standard Korean terms or simple typos, an omitted word, inconsistency of drawing numerals, and irregularities from which the applicant's original intention can be clearly found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the applicant's intention is not clearly understood, ex‑officio amendment is not permitted. The list is illustrative and specific examples follow in numbered items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misspelled words amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious misspellings in violation of Korean grammar may be corrected ex‑officio (example: 'Semiconducter' → 'Semiconductor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical editorial misspellings in the description or claims; must be obviously incorrect and corrected to the intended term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing word obvious in grammar amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: An omitted word that is obvious in the grammar can be added ex‑officio (example: 'signal transmitted ○ line' → 'signal transmitted to line').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only where the missing word is evident from grammar and context so applicant intention is clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency in reference numerals amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Inconsistencies between reference numerals in the description and drawings can be corrected ex‑officio (example: Buffer (115) vs Buffer (15)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change only when one numeral is clearly erroneous and the intended numeral is evident from disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant writing amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Obvious redundant text (e.g., repeated phrase) may be corrected ex‑officio (example: 'The patent office, the patent office is' → 'The patent office is').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove clearly redundant repetitions that do not affect meaning or scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in simple explanation of drawings amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Errors such as misstated figure numbers or misspelled reference numerals in drawing explanations can be corrected ex‑officio (examples: wrong figure numbering; '3…Gear' vs '3…Motor').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must ensure correction does not introduce new technical matter; be careful with drawings to avoid adding unintended subject‑matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong indication of the representative figure amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: If the representative figure is obviously wrongly indicated considering the disclosure, the examiner may correct the representative figure indication ex‑officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction only when obvious from the specification and drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistency in title between description and application amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner may amend the invention title in the description to correspond to the title in the application; if the application's title is inappropriate under rules, examiner may amend it to a proper title and adjust the description title correspondingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the correction ex‑officio button on Patent Net; ensure resulting title meets Part II, Chapter 2 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations to deleted claims — correcting antecedent references
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a deleted claim is cited and only one antecedent claim exists, or where deleted claims are cited among remaining claims, antecedent references should be adjusted ex‑officio to point to surviving antecedent claims (examples provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change citation targets so antecedent references remain valid and clear; only where the correct antecedent is obvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim subject matter mismatch — convert form to match antecedent
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dependent claim cites a claim of a different category (e.g., method dependent on apparatus), the dependent claim may be reworded ex‑officio to match the citing claim type (example given: change 'A method according to claim 1' to 'An apparatus according to claim 1').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only when the intended subject‑matter is evident from the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining dependent claim into cited claim (and deleting duplicates)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a dependent claim is combined into the cited claim (e.g., Claim 1 becomes 'including A and B') the original dependent claim should be deleted ex‑officio to avoid duplication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure deletions are obvious housekeeping and do not alter claim scope beyond correcting redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identical element referred by multiple terms — unify terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the same element is referred to by two or more terms (typo/inconsistent term), examiner may harmonize the wording ex‑officio (example: 'nuclear creation layer' → 'nucleation layer').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change only to the clearly intended, consistent term used elsewhere in the disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obvious wrong claim citation amendable ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: If it's obvious that a claim cites the wrong antecedent claim, the citation may be corrected to the correct antecedent (examples provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction only when the intended antecedent is unambiguous from the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deletion of literally identical repeated claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an identical claim is presented repeatedly, the redundant duplicates may be deleted ex‑officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to remove literal duplication; ensure deletion does not change the intended protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting non‑alternative citation phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims cite multiple claims but intended meaning is alternative (or), the examiner may change phrasing to make alternative meaning explicit (example: 'according to claims 1 and 2' → 'according to claim 1 or 2').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rephrase to reflect intended logical relationship among cited claims; use 'any one of claims 1 to 3' for lists where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification procedure for intended ex‑officio amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must notify the matters to be amended ex‑officio to the applicant with a certified copy of the decision to grant, describing in definite and specific manners which matters are to be amended and stating the reason to help the applicant decide whether to accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate specific paragraph and line numbers so the applicant is not confused; include clear examples such as line/paragraph and corrected wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant opposition and legal effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant opposes acceptance of parts or all of the ex‑officio amendment, they may submit argument before payment of patent fee and select which amended matters they accept; parts objected to are deemed not to have been made and the decision to grant is deemed revoked (except if only abstract amendments are rejected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where ex‑officio amendments are deemed not made, examiner shall re‑examine the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re‑examination timeline after non‑acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: For ex‑officio amendments other than abstracts that are not accepted, the examiner shall re‑examine the application within 1 month from transmission of the written argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If re‑examination finds no grounds for rejection, grant or registration shall be made; ex‑officio amendments contested originally shall not be made again. If re‑examination finds grounds, notify the ground for rejection (again) unless prior notification covers it, in which case examiner may reject without further notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: do not change claim scope by ex‑officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex‑officio amendment must not change the scope of the claims; if there is any possibility that claim terms may be construed to a different meaning, ex‑officio amendment should not be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be conservative — even slight ambiguity that may affect claim construction prohibits ex‑officio amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify ex‑officio matters together when notifying grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When grounds for rejection are notified, matters appropriate for ex‑officio amendment should be notified all together so the applicant may amend accordingly; obvious errors failing description requirements should be notified as grounds for rejection, simple typos as examiner advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separately categorize description‑requirement errors (as grounds) vs simple typos (as advice) to avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add new matter when amending ex‑officio
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must be careful not to add new matters not disclosed in the original description or drawings by ex‑officio amendment, particularly avoiding unintended new technical subject‑matter in drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid introducing any content that would broaden or alter disclosure beyond what was originally filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant intention must be clear principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if an obvious error is apparent, if the applicant's intention is not clearly understood from the specification and written arguments, ex‑officio amendment is not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: where a claim cites only deleted claims and multiple antecedent claims exist and it's not obvious which was intended, do not amend ex‑officio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling partial non‑acceptance of ex‑officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not accept parts of ex‑officio amendment, those parts shall be deemed not to have been made while the other parts remain; ensure remaining parts are not later notified as grounds for rejection and confirm reflected in final amendment if decision to grant is remade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other parts are not reflected in the final amendment, ex‑officio amendment should be made again as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting number of claims after ex‑officio deletions
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims are deleted ex‑officio (e.g., because more than two claims are literally identical), the number of claims shall be corrected ex‑officio on the Patent Net interface for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative housekeeping to keep the claim count consistent with deletions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacing main drawing by ex‑officio amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant did not or wrongly establish a main drawing that explains the claimed invention, the examiner can replace the main drawing ex‑officio by another that better explains the subject matter of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement must not introduce new technical matter; use to improve clarity of original disclosure when a better existing drawing in the file is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re‑notice of ground for rejection — conditions permitting re‑notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may re‑notify the same ground for rejection (instead of immediate rejection) when (①) the purport and content of an amendment to address the ground are clearly indicated in the written argument, (②) the amendment is omitted from the written amendment submitted, (③) if the amendment would have been included the ground would be deemed overcome, and (④) other outstanding grounds are traversed except the omitted one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type of re‑notice must match original (non‑final/final). For applicants without representatives, where only condition ① is met, examiner may re‑notify if necessary to give opportunity to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination promotes accurate substantive examination and early allowance by sharing opinions between examiner and applicant through an interview before substantive examination, allowing discussion of potential grounds for rejection and amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps applicants understand examiner concerns and allows examiners technical explanations to improve accuracy of later substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications eligible include those an examiner has determined to expedite examination and those in technical classifications requiring higher-than-average difficulty; PPH cases may be included when examiner decides to expedite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner uses a determination screen on Patent Net to assess degree of difficulty; eligibility also influenced by expedited examination decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may request preliminary examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant or an agent may request preliminary examination; request must be filed within 14 days from date of sending decision of expedited examination (and not if an office action has already been issued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request via Patent‑Ro (Request for application → Request for preliminary examination); applicant must provide petitioner info, application number, desired interview date(s), participants, contact number, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may participate in the preliminary examination interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants who can attend include the applicant (or corporate representative), an agent, a subagent authorized by applicant/agent, and an inventor; for agent‑handled applications the agent must participate; for assignments to assistant examiners the supervising examiner shall participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should have responsibility to respond to the application; identity verification required for unpublished applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and scope of preliminary examination interview
rubrics_metrics.description: All matters may be discussed: applicant explains technical contents and differences from prior art; examiner explains preliminary review on patentability and deficiencies; both discuss how to amend to resolve grounds for rejection and secure proper scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may present prototypes or multimedia; examiner may give non‑binding suggestions for amendment; main content should be substantive, not mere status questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request timing and desired interview scheduling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should present 3 desired interview dates within a 3‑ to 6‑week window from the request date to allow time for preparation; if examiner issues office action prior to the request, interview is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner requires prior art search, schedule should be after about one month to allow preview based on search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner decision process for accepting or returning request
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner must decide to accept or reject a preliminary examination request within 7 days of the request; requirements include application difficulty, expedited decision status, request timing, participant presence, and appropriate desired dates. Examiner may return a request that fails requirements and cannot be corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if one requirement is not met, examiner may consult with applicant to correct grounds for return; examiner may ex‑officio accept if grounds can be resolved by discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay or cancellation rules for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant causes unavoidable delay, examiner shall offer one more chance to set an available interview date (within the 3–6 week window); if applicant's grounds for delay are unacceptable, the interview can be canceled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of change must be given to applicant when rescheduling once; cancellation if unacceptable reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation required of examiner before interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall read the claimed invention, review patentability requirements and specification deficiencies with preparation comparable to substantive examination, and prepare documents such as prior art search results, minutes of interview, and additional papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State results of preview of grounds for rejection in the minutes to guide discussion during interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and security of participants at interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner shall identify each participant before beginning interview (check ID for unpublished applications); if participant refuses identity checks, limit the interview or restrict content; if participant differs from applicant, interview may be halted/delayed/limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interview is in government complex requiring ID deposit, check identity before entry; maintain confidentiality and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant technical presentation and permitted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may give a technical explanation of the claimed invention and freely use prototypes or multimedia (photos, videos) to help examiner understand; examiner may require presentation materials in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should submit suggested preliminary amendments at least 14 days before the interview for examiner review; examiner may refuse to opine on submissions filed after that period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of suggested preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may explain suggested preliminary amendments (based on self review or prior art search); examiner may give opinions on suggested amendments within allowed scope to assist rapid and accurate examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested amendments should be submitted at least 14 days before interview; voluntary amendments should be filed at least 14 days before interview—late filings may not be considered if examiner has completed preview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative prior‑art explanation and applicant arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may present comparative explanations between the claimed invention and prior art and argue patentability based on differences, using prior art search results submitted when requesting expedited examination or third‑party search reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior art search results to frame differences and patentability arguments during interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner explanation of grounds for rejection and amendment suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners shall explain results of their preliminary review on patentability and specification deficiencies and actively suggest proper ways to resolve grounds for rejection during the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner suggestions are non‑binding; the examiner must explain that the suggestion has no legal binding force and can change according to new prior art or later amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on non‑substantive matters in interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Simple contacts about progress, questions about prosecution process, and procedural matters may be included but must not be the main content of the preliminary examination interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the interview on substantive patentability issues and amendments to improve examination accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minutes of interview required content and signing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant and examiner shall prepare and sign minutes after the interview; minutes must include interview date, place, application number, title, participant names, examiner's opinion on grounds for rejection, suggestions of amendment discussed, and applicant arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signed minutes are uploaded to Patent Net and added to the examination history; it is sufficient to state the purpose of grounds for rejection in the minutes (oral explanation during interview is primary). Suggestions of amendment discussed should be recorded, including any agreed language where applicable.
